{{Short description|Class of norms in additive combinatorics}}
{{redirect|Uniformity norm|the function field norm|uniform norm|uniformity in topology|uniform space}}
In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[additive combinatorics]], a '''Gowers norm''' or '''uniformity norm''' is a class of [[Norm (mathematics)|norms]] on [[function (mathematics)|functions]] on a finite [[Group (mathematics)|group]] or group-like object which quantify the amount of structure present, or conversely, the amount of [[randomness]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-catch-a-pattern-by-figuring-out-how-to-avoid-it-20191125/|title=Mathematicians Catch a Pattern by Figuring Out How to Avoid It|last=Hartnett|first=Kevin|website=Quanta Magazine|date=25 November 2019 |access-date=2019-11-26}}</ref> They are used in the study of [[arithmetic progression]]s in the group.  They are named after [[Timothy Gowers]], who introduced it in his work on [[Szemerédi's theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|authorlink=Timothy Gowers|first=Timothy|last=Gowers|title=A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem|journal=[[Geometric & Functional Analysis]]|volume=11|issue=3|pages=465–588|url=http://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~wtg10/sz898.dvi|year=2001|mr=1844079|doi=10.1007/s00039-001-0332-9|s2cid=124324198 }}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let <math>f</math> be a [[complex number|complex]]-valued function on a finite [[abelian group]] <math>G</math> and let <math>J</math> denote [[complex conjugation]].  The Gowers <math>d</math>-norm is

:<math>\Vert f \Vert_{U^d(G)}^{2^d} = \sum_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_d \in G} \prod_{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d \in \{0,1\}} J^{\omega_1+\cdots+\omega_d} f\left({x + h_1\omega_1 + \cdots + h_d\omega_d}\right) \ .</math>

Gowers norms are also defined for complex-valued functions ''f'' on a segment <math>[N] = {0, 1, 2, ..., N - 1}</math>, where ''N'' is a positive [[integer]]. In this context, the uniformity norm is given as <math>\Vert f \Vert_{U^d[N]} = \Vert \tilde{f} \Vert_{U^d(\mathbb{Z}/\tilde{N}\mathbb{Z})}/\Vert 1_{[N]} \Vert_{U^d(\mathbb{Z}/\tilde{N}\mathbb{Z})}</math>, where <math>\tilde N</math> is a large integer, <math>1_{[N]} </math> denotes the [[indicator function]] of [''N''], and <math>\tilde f(x)</math> is equal to <math>f(x)</math>  for  <math>x \in [N]</math> and <math> 0 </math> for all other <math>x</math>. This definition does not depend on <math>\tilde N</math>, as long as <math>\tilde N > 2^d N</math>.

== Inverse conjectures ==

An ''inverse conjecture'' for these norms is a statement asserting that if a [[bounded function]] ''f'' has a large Gowers ''d''-norm then ''f'' correlates with a polynomial phase of degree ''d'' −&thinsp;1 or other object with polynomial behaviour (e.g. a (''d'' −&thinsp;1)-step [[nilsequence]]). The precise statement depends on the Gowers norm under consideration.

The Inverse Conjecture for [[vector space]]s over a [[finite field]] <math>\mathbb F</math> asserts that for any <math>\delta > 0</math> there exists a constant <math>c > 0</math> such that for any [[dimension (vector space)|finite-dimensional]] vector space ''V'' over <math>\mathbb F</math> and any complex-valued function <math>f</math> on <math>V</math>, bounded by 1, such that <math>\Vert f \Vert_{U^{d}[V]} \geq \delta</math>, there exists a polynomial sequence <math> P \colon V \to \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} </math> such that 

:<math>\left| \frac{1}{|V|} \sum_{x \in V} f(x) e \left( -P(x) \right) \right| \geq c ,</math>

where <math> e(x) := e^{2 \pi i x} </math>. This conjecture was proved to be true by Bergelson, Tao, and Ziegler.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bergelson | first1=Vitaly | last2=Tao | first2=Terence | author2-link = Terence Tao | last3=Ziegler | first3=Tamar | author3-link = Tamar Ziegler | title=An inverse theorem for the uniformity seminorms associated with the action of <math>\mathbb{F}_p^\infty</math> | mr=2594614 | journal=[[Geometric & Functional Analysis]] | year=2010 | volume=19 | issue=6 | pages=1539–1596 | doi=10.1007/s00039-010-0051-1| arxiv=0901.2602 | s2cid=10875469 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tao | first1=Terence | author1-link = Terence Tao | last2=Ziegler | first2=Tamar | author2-link = Tamar Ziegler | title=The inverse conjecture for the Gowers norm over finite fields via the correspondence principle | year=2010 | journal=Analysis & PDE | volume=3 | issue=1 | pages=1–20 | doi=10.2140/apde.2010.3.1 | mr=2663409| arxiv=0810.5527 | s2cid=16850505 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| doi = 10.1007/s00026-011-0124-3
| title = The Inverse Conjecture for the Gowers Norm over Finite Fields in Low Characteristic
| journal = [[Annals of Combinatorics]]
| volume = 16
| pages = 121–188
| year = 2011
| last1 = Tao | first1 = Terence | author1-link = Terence Tao
| last2 = Ziegler | first2 = Tamar | author2-link = Tamar Ziegler
| mr = 2948765
| arxiv = 1101.1469| s2cid = 253591592

The Inverse Conjecture for Gowers <math>U^{d}[N]</math> norm asserts that for any <math> \delta > 0 </math>, a finite collection of (''d'' −&thinsp;1)-step ''[[nilmanifolds]]'' <math>\mathcal{M}_\delta</math> and constants <math>c, C</math> can be found, so that the following is true. If <math> N </math> is a positive integer and <math>f\colon [N]\to \mathbb{C}</math> is bounded in absolute value by 1 and <math> \Vert f \Vert_{U^{d}[N]} \geq \delta </math>, then there exists a nilmanifold <math> G/\Gamma \in \mathcal{M}_\delta </math> and a [[nilsequence]] <math>F(g^nx)</math> where <math>g \in G,\ x \in G/\Gamma</math> and <math>F\colon G/\Gamma \to \mathbb{C}</math> bounded by 1 in absolute value and with Lipschitz constant bounded by <math> C </math> such that:

:<math>\left| \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n =0}^{N-1} f(n) \overline{ F(g^nx}) \right| \geq c .</math>

This conjecture was proved to be true by Green, Tao, and Ziegler.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Green | first1 = Ben | author1-link = Ben Green (mathematician)
| last2 = Tao | first2 = Terence | author2-link = Terence Tao
| last3 = Ziegler | first3 = Tamar | author3-link = Tamar Ziegler
| title = An inverse theorem for the Gowers <math>U^{s+1}[N]</math>-norm
| journal = Electron. Res. Announc. Math. Sci.
| volume = 18
| year = 2011
| pages = 69–90
| doi = 10.3934/era.2011.18.69
| mr = 2817840
| arxiv = 1006.0205}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| doi = 10.4007/annals.2012.176.2.11
| title = An inverse theorem for the Gowers <math>U^{s+1}[N]</math>-norm
| journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]
| volume = 176
| issue = 2
| pages = 1231–1372
| year = 2012
| last1 = Green | first1 = Ben | author1-link = Ben Green (mathematician)
| last2 = Tao | first2 = Terence | author2-link = Terence Tao
| last3 = Ziegler | first3 = Tamar | author3-link = Tamar Ziegler
| mr = 2950773
| arxiv = 1009.3998
| s2cid = 119588323
}}
</ref> It should be stressed that the appearance of nilsequences in the above statement is necessary. The statement is no longer true if we only consider polynomial phases.
